h1: The Lake Hotel Khon Kaen — A Villa-Style Hotel by a Quiet Lakeside in Lao Nadi, Khon Kaen
intro: If you're driving into Khon Kaen yourself and want somewhere quiet, with big rooms right by a waterside garden, without fighting anyone for parking in the city center — The Lake Hotel Khon Kaen is the name guests in this area bring up most often for its quiet and its spacious, good-value rooms · This 56-room villa-style hotel sits beside a small lake in town, in the Lao Nadi Road area, Mueang Kao subdistrict, near the ring road · The highlight is the marble-floor rooms — spacious, with a balcony and a free minibar in every room, and some Villa Suites that come with a jacuzzi · There's large free parking and a waterside garden to sit and relax in · from about THB 1,000/night · scored 7.4 from 16 reviews on Trip.com and 3.8 out of 5 on Tripadvisor

body.html: Who The Lake Hotel suits — To put it as briefly as possible, The Lake Hotel Khon Kaen is a hotel for people driving into Khon Kaen themselves who value quiet, spacious rooms, and easy parking more than staying right by the downtown shopping district · It isn't a high-rise in the business district, and it isn't an arty boutique selling bold design, but a mid-sized 56-room hotel laid out as a cluster of villa-style buildings beside a small lake in the Lao Nadi Road area, near the ring road · What sets it apart from many hotels in town is the quieter, more private feel, with a garden and water as the backdrop, which makes it relaxing in a way that's closer to a small resort than a typical city hotel · Real reviews line up on this: the people it suits are families and groups of friends driving in who want plenty of parking, couples who want a quiet room away from the main road, people here on business or for an event near the Khon Kaen convention center, and travelers who want a spacious, good-value room on a budget of around a thousand-plus baht · Another group that says they were impressed is people stopping over while driving through Khon Kaen, since being near the ring road makes getting in and out of the city easy · You could call it a hotel that plays on the idea of "big, quiet rooms at an accessible price," which is why many people choose to come back, but it's also a hotel you need to understand the style of before booking to be happiest with it

Location and getting around — The Lake Hotel's location is both a selling point and something to weigh up at the same time · The hotel is at 666 Moo 8, Lao Nadi Road, Mueang Kao subdistrict, Mueang Khon Kaen district, a fairly quiet area out toward the edge of town near the ring road · The upside is that getting in and out of the city and driving on to other spots is smooth, traffic isn't as bad as downtown, and there's plenty of space, which keeps the hotel itself quiet, without the constant traffic noise of a hotel on a main road · Distances to key spots aren't far either: around 4-5 min drive to Ton Tan Market and about 5-10 min drive to Central Plaza Khon Kaen · about 3 km to the Khon Kaen International Convention and Exhibition Center (KICE) · about 6 km to Khon Kaen railway station, and Khon Kaen Airport (KKC) is about 10 km away, or roughly 15-20 min drive · One point reviews agree on is that even though it's within the city, the location is out toward the edge — it's not right by the food-and-drink scene like Khao Niao Road or next to a big mall, so if you're not driving yourself, walking anywhere around the hotel isn't very convenient and you mostly rely on Grab or taxis, which during some stretches aren't as quick to hail as in the city center · This makes the hotel clearly better suited to people driving themselves than to those traveling by public transport

"Very spacious room, clean marble floors, lots of parking so no worries, quiet at the back with a lake, a nice relaxing atmosphere · breakfast was decent, close to the airport, very convenient when you drive yourself"

Room types and decor — The Lake Hotel has 56 rooms in total, split into several tiers · It starts with standard rooms and the Family Room for families, starting at around a thousand-plus baht · It steps up to the Pool Access Room in the zone next to the water-garden area, and higher-tier rooms like the Suite Room and Villa Suite, which are much larger, some with a four-poster bed and an in-room jacuzzi · The thing reviews mention most about the rooms is the spaciousness and marble floors — many people say the rooms are bigger than expected for this price, the marble floors look clean and feel cool, the ceilings are high, and there's a private balcony · Rooms have air conditioning, a TV, a fridge with a free minibar (a point many praise), drinking water, a work desk, and an en-suite bathroom with a water heater · The decor leans toward plain and classic rather than boldly modern, focused on space and practicality · But to be straight about it, reviews of the rooms are fairly split — the positive side says the rooms are clean, spacious, and well kept, while the negative side says some rooms show signs of age given the building has been open since 2015, with some reviews mentioning water leaks in the bathroom or rooms that don't match the photos online · The inconsistency between rooms is worth knowing in advance, and it's the reason why choosing a slightly higher room type, or checking the room's condition at check-in, helps a lot

Facilities and the pool question — The pool needs to be addressed clearly from the start, because the information conflicts across platforms · Trip.com and some booking sources list "no swimming pool," while Google Hotels and some sites list an outdoor pool, and the hotel itself genuinely has a room type called Pool Access · To be upfront, the safest reality is that the pool status here is uncertain and reported inconsistently — it may be a small pool in the water-garden zone, or it may be closed during some periods — so if a pool matters for your trip, you should contact the hotel directly to confirm before every booking and not rely on the website photos alone · As for facilities that can be confirmed clearly, there's large free parking, which is what people driving themselves praise most, a lakeside garden and a garden bar to sit and catch the breeze, an on-site restaurant, a 24-hour front desk, daily housekeeping, luggage storage, room service, and free Wi-Fi in both the rooms and common areas that many reviews say has a good signal · Overall the facilities focus on simplicity and quiet relaxation by the water, suited to a one- or two-night stay while sightseeing or running errands in Khon Kaen rather than being a resort destination where you'd spend the whole day in the hotel

Food and dining — The hotel has an on-site restaurant open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner, with room service during some hours · Breakfast is served from about 7:00-10:00 AM and is a point that gets fairly consistent praise — many reviews say breakfast is well done, with a variety of Thai dishes to choose from that taste good and are worth the price · Some reviews even rate breakfast as one of the main pluses of staying here · That said, you should check clearly when booking whether your room rate includes breakfast, because some platforms list it as an add-on you pay extra for · For other meals, since the location is out toward the edge of town, there aren't as many restaurant options within walking distance of the hotel as in the city center, but if you've driven yourself you can drive to Ton Tan Market or into Central Plaza in a few minutes, so it's not a big problem for those with a car · The garden bar by the water is another nice spot for an evening drink in a quiet setting · Overall, The Lake Hotel does well on food when it comes to breakfast, while for other meals it suits heading out to eat if you've driven yourself

Service — Service at The Lake Hotel is another fairly split point in reviews · On the praise side, many reviews say the staff are friendly, smiling, attentive, and helpful with parking and information around town, and the 24-hour front desk makes people arriving late or checking in off-hours more at ease · On the watch-out side, to be straight about it, some voices in reviews mention that staff's English communication is still limited, and there are concerns about consistency of cleaning, with one international reviewer recounting a multi-night stay where the bed linens weren't changed as expected · There's also the phrase "a little soulless" appearing in some reviews, which reflects that the place focuses on convenience and spacious rooms more than being a hotel with a warm, distinctive atmosphere · Overall the service is still decent for a hotel at this price, but consistency is something to set your expectations about realistically

What real reviews say (the good and the bad) — Pulling from Trip.com, Tripadvisor, Agoda, and Hotels.com, the picture that emerges is fairly consistent · On the praise side: spacious rooms and clean-looking marble floors, large free parking ideal for people driving themselves, a quiet atmosphere at the back by the lake and garden, good-tasting breakfast with a variety of Thai dishes, a free minibar in the room, a good Wi-Fi signal, and a location near the airport and the ring road that makes getting in and out of the city easy · On the watch-out side: the thing mentioned most often is the location out toward the edge of town — without a car, getting into the city center and the food-and-drink scene is hard · Next is the inconsistency in room condition — some rooms are nice and clean like the photos, but some reviews ran into rooms older than expected, with water leaks in the bathroom, or conditions not matching the photos online — plus consistency of cleaning and linen changes, staff's still-limited English communication, the pool status with information conflicting across sources, and an overall sense for some people that it "lacks soul" even though it's convenient and good value · Most of these criticisms are manageable by choosing a slightly higher room type, checking the room's condition at check-in, and setting your expectations to match the hotel's style

"The suite was very spacious, had a jacuzzi and a comfy four-poster bed, lots of parking, a quiet atmosphere · the only downside is it's a bit far from the city, so without a car you have to call a Grab, and some parts of the room are starting to show age, but overall great value"

Price and value — Starting rates here are around THB 1,000/night at normal pricing (during some promotions or on weekdays it can drop to around THB 700-800) for standard rooms and the Family Room · Higher-tier rooms like the Suite and Villa Suite, which are much larger and have a jacuzzi, fall in the range of about THB 1,500-2,500 and up depending on size and timing · Compared with similar-tier hotels in Khon Kaen, which are mostly buildings in the commercial district, The Lake Hotel feels good value in terms of room size and quiet, because you get a spacious room, marble floors, a balcony, a free minibar, and large free parking, at a price not far off a typical city hotel · The things that make you weigh it up are the location and the inconsistency in room condition, so the value depends on what you prioritize · If you're driving yourself, want a big quiet room on a budget of around a thousand-plus baht, and aren't fussed about walking to the food-and-drink scene, the money you spend pays off well in terms of space and quiet · But if you prioritize being close to malls and the food-and-drink scene, or want room condition guaranteed to be new and like the photos in every room, you might need to weigh it against a downtown hotel at a similar price instead

Things to know before booking — Several things help make the stay smoother · One, it's best suited to people driving themselves, because the location is out toward the edge of town by the lake, near the ring road — without a car, hailing a Grab during some stretches isn't as quick as downtown, so plan your transport ahead · Two, if a pool matters for your trip, contact the hotel directly before booking, because the pool information conflicts across platforms — don't rely on the website photos alone · Three, if you want to avoid the inconsistency in room condition, choose a slightly higher room type like the Suite or Villa Suite, and check the room's condition at check-in; if it doesn't match what you booked, ask to switch right away · Four, check clearly whether your room rate includes breakfast, and note there's a key-card deposit of about THB 200 that's refunded at check-out · Five, make the most of the waterside setting by sitting in the garden or at the lakeside bar in the evening · Six, during major Khon Kaen events like the Silk Festival and city festivals, rooms fill up fast and prices climb, so book ahead and choose a free-cancellation option if your plans aren't firm

The verdict — From all the real reviews, The Lake Hotel Khon Kaen is the best fit for people driving into Khon Kaen themselves who want a big, quiet room by a waterside garden, with large free parking, on an affordable budget · The marble-floor rooms that are bigger than the price suggests, the free minibar, good-tasting breakfast, and the quiet atmosphere at the back by the lake make it good value in terms of space and quiet for those with a car · If you're looking for the convenience of being right by malls and the downtown food-and-drink scene, want room condition guaranteed to be new and like the photos in every room, or insist on definitely having a pool to use, this might not be the answer, and you should consider a downtown hotel or confirm the pool situation clearly first · But for a Khon Kaen trip where you've driven yourself, want a spacious good-value room, quiet by the water, and a location near the ring road and the airport that makes getting in and out of the city easy — The Lake Hotel is a choice that answers that need well, with the caveat that you should pick your room and set your expectations to match its style

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The Lake Hotel Khon Kaen

faq.q: Where is The Lake Hotel Khon Kaen · what's nearby?
faq.a: It's located at 666 Moo 8, Lao Nadi Road, Mueang Kao subdistrict, Mueang Khon Kaen district, a quiet area out toward the edge of town, near the ring road · around 4-5 min drive to Ton Tan Market and about 5-10 min drive to Central Plaza Khon Kaen · about 3 km to the Khon Kaen convention center (KICE), about 6 km to the railway station, and about 10 km to Khon Kaen Airport (15-20 min drive)

faq.q: What's the starting price at The Lake Hotel Khon Kaen · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 1,000/night for standard rooms and the Family Room at normal pricing (during some promotions it can drop to around THB 700-800) · there are Pool Access Rooms, Suite Rooms, and Villa Suites that are larger and come with a jacuzzi and a four-poster bed, priced from about THB 1,400-2,500 and up · prices climb quickly during city events and high season, so compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Does The Lake Hotel Khon Kaen have a swimming pool?
faq.a: The pool information conflicts across platforms — some booking sources (such as Trip.com) list no pool, while some sources and Google Hotels list an outdoor pool, and the hotel has a room type called Pool Access · to be sure, contact the hotel directly before booking if a pool is important for your trip, and don't rely on the website photos alone

faq.q: Is it convenient to get to The Lake Hotel · should I drive myself?
faq.a: The location is out toward the edge of town by the lake, near the ring road, not by the shopping district or Khao Niao Road · if you're not driving yourself, hailing a car during some stretches isn't as quick as downtown, so it's best to drive yourself or rent a car, and the hotel has large free parking · the upside is being near the ring road and the airport, making it easy to get in and out of the city and drive on to other spots

faq.q: What are the rooms at The Lake Hotel like · is the room condition good?
faq.a: The rooms get praise for being spacious, with clean-looking marble floors, a balcony and a free minibar in every room, and some suites have a jacuzzi and a four-poster bed · but reviews say room condition is inconsistent — some rooms are nice like the photos, while some are older than expected or have water leaks in the bathroom · it's best to choose a slightly higher room type and check the room's condition at check-in; if it doesn't match what you booked, ask to switch right away

faq.q: Who is The Lake Hotel Khon Kaen best suited to?
faq.a: Very well suited to families, couples, and groups of friends driving themselves who want a big, quiet room by a waterside garden, with large free parking, on an affordable budget, and to people here on business or for an event near the Khon Kaen convention center · less suited to people who want a location right by malls and the downtown food-and-drink scene, don't have their own car, or insist on definitely having a pool to use
